Built against [wamsoft/krkrz_dev](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_dev) V2.6.5

- **Live2D characters**: a World character can be a Live2D Cubism model, posed by its motions, with faces that fade into each other, blinking and lip-sync to its voice (`doc/world.txt`, "Live2D Characters"). Hiyori, Live2D Inc.'s sample model, joins the Animated Character demo
- **The Live2D plugin is built with your own Cubism SDK**: Live2D's licence keeps its Cubism Core out of these packages, so `tools/live2d/setup.py` (in the repository) walks you through building krkrlive2d for Windows, Linux, macOS, Android and iOS. The web doesn't have Live2D yet
- **kagex-release: a game's own plugins**: libraries in `plugins/windows`, `plugins/linux` or `plugins/macos` next to `data/` go into that platform's packages
- kagex-release 0.13.0 downloads the 0.13.0 engines

The sample game with Live2D, where this release has it (`kagex_sample_live2d_<platform>`), holds Live2D's Cubism Core: by installing or playing it you agree not to copy the Cubism Core out of it, distribute it apart from the game, modify it, or reverse engineer, decompile or disassemble it. It uses sample data owned and copyrighted by Live2D Inc.

Everything in this release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.13.0/CHANGELOG.md).

On Windows the engine needs OpenGL ES: a graphics driver that supports it, or ANGLE's `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` next to `krkrz.exe`.

The macOS app and tools aren't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time: open the app from the context menu (Open), or allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security; for the tools, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine kagex-release kagex-lipsync`. The Android APK is signed with a debug key: allow installs from unknown sources, or use `adb install`. The sample's iOS build is for the Simulator; kagex-release signs a game for iPhones and iPads with your own Apple Developer certificate.
